Subject: Renewal: capacity top-up, logical tenancy & throughput guarantees (Helix Analytics)

Hi Kara / Helix procurement,

Thanks again for the productive renewal conversation last week. To recap the proposal we discussed for your Q4 renewal: we will add a reserved pool of 16 additional A100-equivalent GPUs scoped to Helix; configure logical tenancy (tenant fencing) at the pool level; and add a throughput SLA (200 RPS sustained / 500 RPS burst) for your mission-critical ingestion pipelines.

Attached: draft amendment (PDF), logical tenancy topology (PNG), and a short throughput addendum (DOCX). Can you confirm the following so our legal and ops teams can finalize the amendment?
- Procurement OK with the term change to 12 months, auto-renew clause toggled off per request
- Acceptance of the dedicated logical tenancy model (no physical host-level tenant guarantees, logical fencing with strict KV/prefix isolation)
- Agreement on the migration window: 2-hour maintenance window during Sunday UTC midnight–02:00 (we proposed July 29)

Next steps: if procurement confirms, I’ll route the DocuSign for signature and loop in Rishi (SRE) and Karthik (account engineering) to schedule the runbook & cutover.

Best,
Michael

Thanks Michael — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Procurement: we can sign a 12-month term with auto-renew off, but we need the pricing locked for 6 months after amendment execution.
2) Logical tenancy: our security team would like a short (one-page) statement describing isolation guarantees for cross-tenant KV cache and prefix caching (we need to show this to compliance).
3) Throughput SLA: 200 RPS sustained sounds reasonable provided there is a documented fallback plan (i.e., degraded latency vs. throttling behavior).
4) Migration window: July 29/00:00–02:00 UTC works for most of the team; can you confirm Rishi/ops availability?

Kara Levin
VP Engineering, Helix Analytics

Subject: RE: Renewal: capacity top-up, logical tenancy & throughput guarantees (Helix Analytics)

Quick ops plan: 
- Pool provisioning: we will provision a 16-GPU reserved pool tagged helix-prd-2028; physical nodes shared across tenants but runtime-level fencing enforced by our control plane and kernel-level prefix isolation.
- KV/prefix isolation: we will enforce per-tenant namespaces in the KV cache and enable strict eviction policies scoped by tenant id. We will produce the one-page isolation statement Marissa offered.
- SLA behavior: default will be (A) throttling to preserve P99 latency; option (B) degraded responses only if customer requests token-priority behavior — we should capture this as a checkbox in the addendum.
- Cutover & verification: 2-hour maintenance window; pre-check (connectivity and credentials), staged routing (10% -> 50% -> 100%), post-cutover smoke tests (embedding correctness, latency p99), and log snapshot for audit.

I’ll own runbook authoring and will post the runbook link to Jira and Confluence. Proposed engineers on-call: rishi.malhotra, neha.kapoor, karthik.iyer.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of SRE, Redwood Inference

- Migration window confirmed: Jul 29, 00:00–02:00 UTC; runbook and on-call confirmed (Rishi, Neha, Karthik)
